# Narrated read and stage actions: report-runner amendment aftermath

This is a narration only. No tools ran. Commands and dispatches are quoted as the actions I would take. Their outcomes come from the case's fixed observations.

## Trace A: main git path

**A1. Required read.** `read` the absolute path `…/skills/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md`, section 5 ("Before the aftermath, `read` this section again"). I also need section 1's predicate and Value decoding, and Standing grants, for the grant re-read in A7. The case gives no observation that this read fails. If it were unreadable, the step would stop with a blocking error and the grammar would not be improvised.

**A2. Ledger check.** The case observes no ledger, so the plan path applies. The plan exists and `plan_check` already returned, so I am at the section 5 return point.

**A3. Attribution check.** There are two outcomes:
- **Second identical `plan_check` FAIL.** The quoted plan text is ``Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` ``. It sits under Task 1, whose `Spec:` anchor is `doc/specs/report-runner.md#tests`, the amended section. `git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD:doc/plans/report-runner.md` shows Task 1's Tests as `` `node --test eval/lib/lint.test.mjs` baseline: 3a8fad8c pass…``. So this batch changed the text, and the FAIL is attributable.
- **First `dirtied tracked source` row.** Its command is the same changed Tests text, so it is attributable too.

Both outcomes form one amend-class item. This is the first aftermath item, under the cap of two, and it repeats no evidence from an already-applied item.

**A4. Redraw check.** The correction moves the Tests line back to final verification. The Goal, Problem, ACs and boundaries are unchanged, so this is amend-class, not a redraw.

**A5. Tracked-membership checks.** Each check runs as a separate command:
```bash
git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
```
- Each command prints its path, so all three are tracked.
- None of them is the spec, the plan, or an `In-flight:` path.
- `artifacts: /tmp/report-runner-artifacts/audit.log` is outside the row and is preserved.

The row is eligible for restore.

**A6. Exact restore, before applying the retry.** These run in the explicit worktree, one quoted path per command:
```bash
git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
```
- Each command exits 0. A nonzero exit would stop the step and print the shell error.
- The orchestrator does this restore itself. It is not delegated, and it is not a general licence to restore test damage.

**A7. Held item.**

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| handle | `replay` |
| title | Move replay to verification |
| location | Tests |
| recommended | `accept` (no `alt-n` exists) |
| evidence | the verbatim lines `FAIL (1 findings)` / `command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token` / ``> Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` ``, plus the dirtied row naming the three paths |

**A8. Grant re-read.** I re-read the spec header through section 1's predicate and Value decoding. It shows `**Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends`, the same value as before. That is amend permission, not budget-only, `none`, or malformed.

Acknowledgment: the standing grant applies, so the recommended edit lands without a menu.

**A9. Apply the edit.** Edit the spec Tests from "replays in Task 1 Tests" to "replays at final verification", then print:
`amended the spec: Move replay to verification - Tests now replays at final verification instead of in Task 1 Tests`

**A10. Re-dispatch the plan-writer.** The dispatch follows writing-plans `## Author the plan` step 3 and carries only this content:
- `Amend:` Tests. The rule sentence reads: "preserve every task title and wave position the amendment does not touch; edit only affected anchors and tasks; resolve: `FAIL (1 findings)` / `command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token` / ``> Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` `` and `Task 1: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json`."
- `In-flight:` doc/specs/report-runner.md, doc/plans/report-runner.md

**A11. Parent check.** Run the parent's steps 5-6 (`plan_check`). The fixed observation is PLAN WRITTEN, then parent `PASS`, with no unrelated failures.

**A12. Final read.** Read `doc/plans/report-runner.md` once. This is step 7's read, without its phase completion or `plan_tracker` init. The main loop never edits the plan text.

**A13. Tracker update.**
- Task 1's anchors changed and it was complete, so reopen it in place: `plan_tracker({ action: "update", index: <Task 1>, status: "in_progress" })`.
- No tasks were added or removed.
- No `phase_tracker` call is made, because the phase stays `implement`.

**A14. One batch commit.** Stage and commit the spec and plan together. The three restored files carry no diff, so they are not part of the commit.
```bash
git -C /tmp/report-worktree add -- doc/specs/report-runner.md doc/plans/report-runner.md && \
git -C /tmp/report-worktree commit -q -F - -- doc/specs/report-runner.md doc/plans/report-runner.md <<'EOF'
amend: 2 item(s) - Run report replay, Move replay to verification

- <earlier handle> | Run report replay | Tests: replays at final verification -> replays in Task 1 Tests | <choice as already recorded> | <reason> | <evidence>
- replay | Move replay to verification | Tests: replays in Task 1 Tests -> replays at final verification | granted | aftermath retry under standing grant | FAIL (1 findings) / command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token / > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`; Task 1 dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json
"auto-apply amends"
EOF
```

**A15. Audit choice kinds.**
- Under the grant, an aftermath item records as `granted`, and the quoted granting sentence goes in the body.
- If there were no grant, the item would go through the sections 2-4 menu. A later human reply records it as `accepted` (letter A) or `alt-n`.
- The finishing digest reads only `auto-apply` and `granted` records.

**A16. Undo.**
1. Run `git -C /tmp/report-worktree revert <batch sha>`. This undoes both items and the retried plan together.
2. Read `**Amend-grant:**` from the pre-revert HEAD with `git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD^:doc/specs/report-runner.md`, through the predicate.
3. If the working tree's value differs, restore that value and persist it per Standing grants.
4. Then re-enter the surface for the items to keep.

## Trace U: untracked test file added to the row

**U1.** `git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "tests/report-new.test.mjs"` prints nothing. The file shows `??` at a `Create:`/`Test:` path, so it is ineligible.

**U2.** The whole row goes through step 6, with no partial restoration. **None of the original three paths is restored.** There is no apply and no re-dispatch.

**U3.** Render the step-6 exit in full, then pause:
- **Task and command:** Task 1, `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`.
- **SHA:** not in the observations.
- **Exit:** not in the observations.
- **Summary:** dirtied tracked source plus a new untracked test file. The cause is that the command ran in Task 1 Tests.

Options:
- `fix-first`
- `narrow`
- `amend`

`Recommendation: amend - move replay back to final verification.`

The human decides whether to commit, discard, or move each of the four paths.

## Trace P: protected path added to the row

**P1.** `doc/specs/report-runner.md` is tracked but protected. The same applies if the extra path is the plan or any other `In-flight:` path.

**P2.** The whole row goes through step 6, as in U2-U3. **None of the original three paths is restored.** There is no apply and no re-dispatch, and the step pauses for the human.

## Trace R: redraw-class second FAIL

**R1.** The FAIL reads `acceptance-scope @ line 24: report runner must also audit refund records…`. Fixing it changes the spec Goal and acceptance criteria. That is redraw-class, and the standing grant never covers a redraw.

**R2.** Before any restore, commit the batch as-is: the spec carrying "Run report replay" plus the plan, in one `amend:` commit with that item's audit. This commit preserves the batch; it is not cleanup.

**R3.** Hand the three dirtied paths to step 6 without restoring them. The human decides to commit, discard, or move each.

**R4.** `read` `…/skills/brainstorming/SKILL.md`, section "Amending an approved spec". If it is unreadable, the step stops with a blocking error.

**R5.** State the redraw call and stop for the user, who may override it.

**R6.** On confirmation, run the redraw:
1. `plan_tracker({ action: "clear" })`
2. `phase_tracker({ action: "reset" })`
3. `phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "brainstorm" })`
4. Delete `doc/plans/report-runner.md`. There is no ledger to delete.
5. Resume at checklist step 4 with the approved spec as the draft.

## Plain-jj restore (equivalent to A6)

Use this instead of the git checkout, never both. `-R` does not root paths, so the fileset is root-anchored:
```bash
jj -R /tmp/report-worktree restore -- 'root:"eval/report-runner/report.md"'
```
Repeat the same form, one command each, for `root:"eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"` and `root:"eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"`.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## Main git trace

1. **Required reference read.** Narrate a fresh read of `<absolute skills root>/brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md`, §5, before running the batch aftermath, and its standing-grant rules before decoding the grant. These are required reads, not claimed live calls; the bundled reference does not count as a session read. If either required read is unreadable, stop with a blocking error rather than reconstructing it.

2. **Attribute the two findings.** The narrated HEAD lookup is:
   ```bash
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree show HEAD:doc/plans/report-runner.md
   ```
   Its fixed observation shows Task 1 previously ran `node --test eval/lib/lint.test.mjs`, whereas this batch introduced `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`. Task 1’s `Spec:` anchor points to the amended Tests section. Both the repeated command-contract failure and the dirty-source row therefore concern text this batch changed—not merely the same task or line number.

   Hold one retry item, not two:
   - **Handle:** replay
   - **Title:** Move replay to verification
   - **Location:** Tests
   - **Correction:** `replays in Task 1 Tests` → `replays at final verification`
   - **Recommendation:** accept; no alternatives
   - **Evidence, verbatim:**
     ```text
     FAIL (1 findings)
     command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token
     > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`
     ```
     ```text
     - Task 1: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json
     ```

   This is an amend-class Tests correction, not a redraw or descope. It is the first aftermath retry item; the batch’s original amendment is not itself an aftermath retry.

3. **Check restore eligibility for the entire row.** Narrate these membership checks:
   ```bash
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree ls-files -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
   ```
   Each fixed observation prints its path. All three are outside the spec, plan, and In-flight protected set. Preserve `/tmp/report-runner-artifacts/audit.log`; it is outside this row and is not cleanup material.

4. **Restore exactly those three paths before applying the retry.** The orchestrator—not the writer—would issue:
   ```bash
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/report.md"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json"
   git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json"
   ```
   Each fixed outcome is exit 0. A nonzero outcome would stop this sequence and report the shell error.

5. **Re-read and acknowledge the grant, then apply.** The narrated spec re-read observes exactly:
   ```text
   **Amend-grant:** auto-apply amends
   ```
   Decode it under the required standing-grant reference. The observed amendment permission authorizes the recommended correction without a human menu; it does not authorize a redraw.

   Narrate the resulting confirmation and edit:
   ```text
   Recorded: replay=accept
   amended the spec: Move replay to verification - move replay from Task 1 Tests to final verification.
   ```

6. **Re-dispatch the writer, then check.** Read the required writing-plans author/check instructions before using that workflow; do not reconstruct unavailable reference contents. The intended `plan-writer` dispatch contains only:
   ```text
   Amend:
   - doc/specs/report-runner.md: Tests
   - Move replay to final verification. Preserve unaffected task titles and
     wave positions; correct the affected Tests contract evidenced by:
     FAIL (1 findings)
     command-contract @ line 24: Tests segment requires a Test: path token
     > Tests: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit`
     - Task 1: `node eval/run.mjs report-runner audit` dirtied tracked source: eval/report-runner/report.md, eval/report-runner/results/audit/baseline.json, eval/report-runner/results/audit/candidate.json

   In-flight:
   - doc/specs/report-runner.md
   - doc/plans/report-runner.md
   ```
   The fixed subsequent observations are `PLAN WRITTEN` and parent `PASS`.

7. **Finalize once, in order.** Read the amended plan once after PASS; the parent does not edit its text. Then update Task 1 from complete to `in_progress`, because its anchors changed. Do not initialize a fresh tracker or complete/change the implement phase.

   Commit spec and plan together once, preserving the original amendment and retry in the audit:
   ```text
   amend: 2 item(s) - Run report replay, Move replay to verification
   ```
   Keep the original item’s actual decision record; record the grant-applied retry as `granted`, with its evidence and granting sentence. A later human-selected correction would instead be audited as `accepted` or `alt-n`, according to the answer—not `granted`.

   To undo, revert this single batch commit. Then read the pre-revert HEAD’s grant through the required predicate/decoder and restore/persist that value if the revert changed it, before reconsidering retained items.

## Independent ineligible-row variants

8. **U — untracked planned test.** Reset to the pre-restore state. The extra `tests/report-new.test.mjs` has `??`, appears under `Create:`/`Test:`, and its membership check prints nothing. The **whole row is ineligible**: restore none of the original three paths. Render the writing-plans dirty-path exit, naming all paths and their cause, and ask the human to commit, discard, or move them. Do not re-dispatch over unresolved dirt.

9. **P — protected path.** Reset independently. Adding the spec—or the plan or another In-flight path—makes the **whole row ineligible**, even when tracked. Again, restore none of the original three paths; hand the entire row to the human without partial restoration.

10. **R — redraw before restoration.** Reset independently. The changed FAIL demands refund-record support outside the Goal and ACs. This is a redraw, not the Tests retry. Before restoring anything, commit the existing batch as-is, preserving it rather than cleaning up source damage. Hand dirty paths to the writing-plans exit without restoration. Then take the redraw route: retain worktree/spec, clear tasks, reset/start brainstorm, delete the plan and any identified loop ledger, and resume checklist step 4. The amendment grant does not replace full spec approval.

## Equivalent plain-jj restore

11. **Eligible main-row example only:**
   ```bash
   jj -R /tmp/report-worktree restore -- 'root:"eval/report-runner/report.md"'
   ```
   Use the root-anchored fileset because `-R` selects the workspace but does not rebase path resolution from the current directory. Use this instead of—not alongside—the corresponding git checkout.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the Change without losing anything Before held. Before failed restore because it collapsed the three paths into one unquoted checkout command and its plain-jj example also bundled three filesets; After splits them into three `git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout -- "<path>"` commands and one root:-anchored jj form per path. Before failed dispatch because the Amend: rule sentence carried no FAIL lines or dirtied row; After quotes both inside the rule sentence while keeping In-flight: and avoiding any Findings: block. Before failed commit because its audit line summarized the evidence (`(x2) + dirtied tracked row`) rather than quoting it verbatim and did not say the revert undoes the retries with the batch; After quotes the FAIL lines and row and states the revert covers both items and the retried plan. Before failed protected and redraw because U/P only 'stop and report' without naming step 6 or commit/discard/move, and R only paused for the human without committing the batch as-is, handing the paths to step 6, or entering the brainstorming redraw; After adds the step-6 exit rendering, the commit-as-is before any restore, and the redraw sequence. Grant held in both. To keep this result, retain the explicit per-path quoted commands, the quoted evidence inside the Amend: rule sentence and commit body, the step-6 routing text for ineligible rows, and the R2→R3→redraw ordering; the only wording to watch in After is U3's 'each of the four paths', which correctly excludes the artifact but should not be broadened.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After moves every fact from fails to holds and nothing regresses. The decisive wording changes were: narrating three separate `ls-files` membership checks followed by three single-quoted-path `git -C /tmp/report-worktree checkout --` commands (Before used one multi-path unquoted checkout and a `cd`-based jj restore with bare paths and no `root:` fileset); attributing the finding explicitly through the HEAD `show` of the prior Task 1 Tests and the amended Spec anchor rather than merely stating the retry was consumed; quoting the FAIL lines and dirtied row inside the Amend block's rule sentence instead of leaving them as external 'retry context'; showing the single `amend: 2 item(s)` batch commit with the retry audited as `granted` plus evidence and granting sentence; sending the U/P rows to the writing-plans dirty-path exit with commit/discard/move and no partial restore (Before only 'surfaced the blocker'); and in R, committing the batch as-is, handing the dirty paths to the exit without restoration, then taking the brainstorming redraw route (Before just stopped for a human decision). To keep these solid, consider naming 'step 6' literally in the U/P/R exits and retaining the explicit 'do not invent a Test: token / do not hand-edit the plan in the parent' sentence from Before inside the dispatch step, since After only implies it; otherwise the After wording delivers the Change without losing anything Before held.
